events.title: Hindenburg Disaster
events.description: The German passenger airship LZ 129 Hindenburg caught fire and was destroyed while attempting to dock at Naval Air Station Lakehurst in New Jersey, killing 36 people (13 passengers, 22 crew members, and one ground crewman).
events.significance: The disaster, captured in dramatic newsreel footage and radio broadcast, ended the era of commercial passenger airships and shattered public confidence in hydrogen-filled rigid airships.

events.title: Roger Bannister Breaks the Four-Minute Mile
events.description: British athlete Roger Bannister ran a mile in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds at the Iffley Road track in Oxford, England, becoming the first person to break the four-minute barrier.
events.significance: The feat was long considered a physical limit of human capability; its achievement redefined athletic possibility and was followed by other runners breaking the barrier within weeks.

events.title: Eiffel Tower Opens to the Public at the Exposition Universelle
events.description: The Eiffel Tower, built as the entrance arch to the 1889 World's Fair in Paris, was opened to the public after its official inauguration in March, with the Exposition Universelle opening on this date.
events.significance: The 300-metre iron structure, initially controversial, became the enduring symbol of Paris and France and a landmark demonstration of modern engineering.

events.title: Birth of Sigmund Freud
events.description: Sigmund Freud, the Austrian neurologist and founder of psychoanalysis, was born in Freiberg, Moravia, then part of the Austrian Empire.
events.significance: Freud's theories of the unconscious mind, dreams, and psychosexual development profoundly shaped psychology, psychiatry, literature, and popular culture in the 20th century.

events.title: Stalin Becomes Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars
events.description: Joseph Stalin assumed the post of Premier of the Soviet Union by becoming Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars, formally adding government leadership to his role as Communist Party General Secretary.
events.significance: The move formalized Stalin's direct control of the state weeks before Germany's invasion of the USSR, and he led the Soviet wartime government through World War II.
